_about: What GitHub has verified about the build files, quoted in the kit guides. Update it after a build passes, then run tools/embed_kit_bundle.py again.
android: Version 3.6 (14 October 2026): the desk is never lost again. A window that opens with an empty store (after an update, or at a new address while an older copy is still open) takes the desk kept on disk instead of writing its empty one over it; the desk on disk keeps a copy each day and before any save that would suddenly shrink it; Settings, Data on this device, Find earlier desks lists those copies and the desks the web view still holds from an earlier address, and restores one. Using another computer's models: Find my other computers searches the home network, and a failed connection says why (on a Mac, the Local Network permission in Privacy & Security). Tested in Chromium on Linux with a stand-in for the desktop bridge. Version 3.5 (14 October 2026): a saved conversation shows its keys, Edit, document cards and times from the moment the app opens (before, they came only after a new message); a round arrow takes the chat to its newest message; each message and reply keeps its time; Fast answers without thinking first on the models on this device; spreadsheets and slide decks made in the chat; the app library; Memory; About lists what is running; and the icon is drawn the same size as Carpe Diem's. Tested in Chromium and WebKit on Linux. When these notes were written, GitHub had not yet built 3.5 for this device. Version 3.4 (13 October 2026) adds Lector (a whole app or long document read with your own model), documents made in the chat (Word, PDF, Markdown), apps and games that run beside the chat and become installable apps, Edit, Try again and versions, and model settings from the house tiles and the chat menu. These were tested in Chromium on Linux. When these notes were written, GitHub had not yet built 3.4 for this device; the paragraph that follows describes 3.3. Version 3.3 was built on GitHub on 13 October 2026 and passed its test on an Android emulator (the built-in model answered a question) before it was published. What changed since, and was tested in Chromium on Linux only: the Code view opens a large page at once; the chat fills the window and matches the live preview; the side buttons move as Carpe Diem's; hover cards and previewed pages read correctly at night. It has not been tried on a physical Fire tablet by me. Version 3.2 (10 October 2026) has not been built on GitHub yet: GitHub's build machines were not available when this kit was made, so these build files have not been run in the cloud for 3.2, and no 3.2 app has been tested on an emulator or a tablet. What was checked for 3.2, on a Linux computer: the app's Java code compiled against Android's version 35 libraries; the engine the app carries read a conversation's instructions ahead, then answered "Paris" with LFM2.5 1.2B Instruct, its first reply taking about 0.32 seconds instead of about 4.0 seconds; the app's page passed its tests in Chromium on Linux, with the real engine (llama.cpp) running LFM2.5 1.2B Instruct where a model was needed: Ingenium's ten rules reach every model's instructions (20 checks) and come before the person's own layer (9 checks); tooltips above each control, in each page's own colours and font (15 checks); the new sticky note papers, Lavender first, with their names (7 checks); pasting from outside through the edit panel (12 checks, with a stand-in for the app's clipboard); the first reply no longer waits for the instructions (5 checks); building your own AI on top of a model (18 checks); the model lineup for each device (45 checks); Support (33 checks); the first-start downloads (24 checks); and the guided tour (22 checks). The converter turned LFM2.5 350M and Gemma 3 270M into F16, Q8_0 and Q4_K_M files identical byte for byte to those of llama.cpp's own converter and quantizer, in the browser, the Fire app and the computer app (27 checks each), and both converted models answered correctly. The paste through Android's own clipboard has not been tried on a device. The last build that passed on GitHub is version 3.1: Ingenium's Android build files were built and tested on GitHub on 9 October 2026 (build 3.1.20261009.18, at commit 4fc394e, with the app's name and id read from app.json): the build checked that the app carries the engine's processor parts, one for each generation of 64-bit ARM chip (from ARMv8.0 to ARMv9.2), so that the engine can load the fastest part a tablet's chip supports when it starts. On an Android emulator, the first built-in model (LFM2.5 1.2B Instruct) answered "Paris" to "What is the capital of France?", the second (LFM2.5 1.2B Thinking) thought before answering "Is 91 a prime number?" and its thinking reached the page, the app reached the internet through itself (a request to Wikipedia returned status 200), and the copy without the models (about 15 MB) installed over the full app and opened. This build is version 3.1 and carries the look approved on 9 October 2026: chat bubbles that rise into place with a small spring when they first appear, lift under the pointer and breathe gently while an answer is being written (minimal motion and the system's reduce-motion setting turn this off); the raised 3D look with light shadows; and no purple glow around the door's seal, the purple keys or the app's icon, by day or by night. The look was checked in Chromium on Linux in day and night, on a computer screen and a phone screen. The guided tour (22 checks), Support (33 checks), the first-start downloads (24 checks) and the live thinking view (10 checks) were tested again in Chromium on Linux on this page. Joining a computer that lends its models was tested in Chromium on Linux against a stand-in computer running the real engine with LFM2.5 1.2B Instruct. The question the model reads is 428 tokens long, because the clear-communication part of Support is added to it; it is read once at the start of each conversation, and Support can switch it off. The emulator is an x86 machine, so it tested how the engine loads its processor part but not the choice between ARM parts; it is also far slower than a tablet, and its speed varies from run to run (it read the 428-token question in about 116 seconds, against about 240 seconds in the build before), so its speeds say nothing about a Fire tablet. Joining a computer's models was not tested from the emulator. The app has not been tried on a physical Fire tablet, so the look of the new animation on one is not yet known.
